mark.14.p1.b1.text: Now the Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread were two days away,

mark.14.p1.b2.text: The chief priests and scribes were looking for a covert way to arrest Jesus and kill Him.

mark.14.p1.b3.text: But not during the feast, … or there may be a riot among the people.

mark.14.p2.b1.text: While Jesus was in Bethany reclining at the table in the home of Simon the Leper,

mark.14.p2.b2.text: A woman came with an alabaster jar of expensive perfume, made of pure nard.

mark.14.p2.b3.text: She broke open the jar and poured it on Jesus’ head.

mark.14.p3.b2.text: It could have been sold for over three hundred denarii and the money given to the poor.

mark.14.p3.b3.text: Leave her alone; why are you bothering her?

mark.14.p3.b4.text: She has done a beautiful deed to Me.

mark.14.p4.b1.text: The poor you will always have with you, and you can help them whenever you want.

mark.14.p4.b2.text: But you will not always have Me.

mark.14.p4.b3.text: She has done what she could to anoint My body in advance of My burial.

mark.14.p4.b4.text: And truly I tell you, wherever the gospel is preached in all the world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her.

mark.14.p5.b1.text: Then Judas Iscariot, one of the Twelve, went to the chief priests

mark.14.p5.b3.text: They were delighted to hear this, and they promised to give him money.

mark.14.p5.b4.text: So Judas began to look for an opportunity to betray Jesus.

mark.14.p6.b1.text: On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, when the Passover lamb was to be sacrificed,

mark.14.p6.b2.text: Where do You want us to prepare for You to eat the Passover?

mark.14.p6.b3.text: Go into the city, and a man carrying a jug of water will meet you.

mark.14.p7.b1.text: The Teacher asks: Where is My guest room, where I may eat the Passover with My disciples?

mark.14.p7.b2.text: And he will show you a large upper room, furnished and ready. Make preparations for us there.

mark.14.p7.b4.text: When evening came, Jesus arrived with the Twelve.

mark.14.p8.b1.text: Truly I tell you, one of you who is eating with Me will betray Me.

mark.14.p8.b3.text: It is one of the Twelve—the one who is dipping his hand into the bowl with Me.

mark.14.p8.b4.text: But woe to that man by whom He is betrayed! It would be better for him if he had not been born.

mark.14.p9.b1.text: Take it; this is My body.

mark.14.p9.b2.text: Then He took the cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them, and they all drank from it.

mark.14.p9.b3.text: This is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many.

mark.14.p9.b4.text: Truly I tell you, I will no longer drink of the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it anew in the kingdom of God.

mark.14.p10.b1.text: You will all fall away, … I will strike the Shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.

mark.14.p10.b2.text: But after I have risen, I will go ahead of you into Galilee.

mark.14.p10.b3.text: Even if all fall away, I never will.

mark.14.p10.b4.text: Truly I tell you, … this very night, before the rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times.

mark.14.p11.b2.text: My soul is consumed with sorrow to the point of death. Stay here and keep watch.

mark.14.p11.b3.text: Abba, Father, … all things are possible for You. Take this cup from Me.

mark.14.p11.b4.text: Yet not what I will, but what You will.

mark.14.p12.b1.text: Simon, are you asleep? … Were you not able to keep watch for one hour?

mark.14.p12.b2.text: Watch and pray so that you will not enter into temptation. For the spirit is willing, but the body is weak.

mark.14.p12.b3.text: That is enough! The hour has come. Look, the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.

mark.14.p12.b4.text: Rise, let us go. See, My betrayer is approaching!

mark.14.p13.b1.text: While Jesus was still speaking, Judas, one of the Twelve, arrived, accompanied by a crowd armed with swords and clubs, sent from the chief priests, scribes, and elders.

mark.14.p13.b2.text: The One I kiss is the man; arrest Him and lead Him away securely.

mark.14.p14.b1.text: Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest Me as you would an outlaw?

mark.14.p14.b2.text: Every day I was with you, teaching in the temple courts, and you did not arrest Me. But this has happened that the Scriptures would be fulfilled.

mark.14.p14.b3.text: Then everyone deserted Him and fled.

mark.14.p15.b1.text: One young man who had been following Jesus was wearing a linen cloth around his body. They caught hold of him,

mark.14.p15.b2.text: But he pulled free of the linen cloth and ran away naked.

mark.14.p15.b3.text: They led Jesus away to the high priest, …

mark.14.p15.b4.text: Peter followed Him at a distance, right into the courtyard of the high priest. And he sat with the officers and warmed himself by the fire.

mark.14.p16.b1.text: Now the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin were seeking testimony against Jesus to put Him to death, but they did not find any.

mark.14.p16.b2.text: We heard Him say, ‘I will destroy this man-made temple, and in three days I will build another that is made without hands.’

mark.14.p16.b3.text: But even their testimony was inconsistent.

mark.14.p17.b1.text: Have You no answer? What are these men testifying against You?

mark.14.p17.b2.text: But Jesus remained silent and made no reply.

mark.14.p17.b3.text: Are You the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?

mark.14.p17.b4.text: I am, … and you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming with the clouds of heaven.

mark.14.p18.b1.text: Why do we need any more witnesses? … You have heard the blasphemy. What is your verdict?

mark.14.p18.b2.text: And they all condemned Him as deserving of death.

mark.14.p18.b4.text: And the officers received Him with slaps in His face.

mark.14.p19.b1.text: While Peter was in the courtyard below, one of the servant girls of the high priest came down

mark.14.p19.b2.text: You also were with Jesus the Nazarene.

mark.14.p19.b3.text: I do not know or even understand what you are talking about,

mark.14.p19.b4.text: Then he went out to the gateway, and the rooster crowed.

mark.14.p20.b1.text: Surely you are one of them, for you too are a Galilean.

mark.14.p20.b2.text: I do not know this man of whom you speak!

mark.14.p20.b3.text: And immediately the rooster crowed a second time.

mark.14.p20.b4.text: Before the rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times.
